title: Resonant Far-Infrared Spectroscopy of Flat-Band Fermions in Magic Angle Graphene
authors: Ayelet J. Uzan-Narovlansky, Ipsita Das, Juan F. Mendez Valderrama, Yue Tang, Jonah Herzog-Arbeitman, Haoyu Hu, Pengjie Wang, Zhaoyi Joy Zheng, Haosen Guan, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, B. Andrei Bernevig, Sanfeng Wu
abstract: Moiré engineering in twisted two-dimensional (2D) materials radically alters low-energy bands, interactions and topological quantum states. Despite extensive studies, optical spectroscopy of interacting moiré bands in the characteristic far-infrared (FIR) regime has remained largely unexplored due to extreme experimental challenges. Using a newly developed millikelvin FIR platform, we report the observation of the long-sought-after characteristic FIR resonances of flat-band electrons in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (MATBG). We observe highly tunable spectroscopic signatures of interacting light and heavy fermions that constitute the flat bands in MATBG. Using the topological heavy-fermion model (THF), we show that itinerant topological electrons act as an "antenna" that couples strongly to the optical field, with resonant frequencies renormalized by the hybridization with localized heavy electrons. We establish optical selection rules of MATBG which uncovers the key symmetry governing light-heavy fermion hybridization. At charge neutrality, we observe pronounced resonances at energies below the on-site Coulomb energy, implying the emergence of new many-body modes. Our experiments and modeling provide a fundamental understanding of light-matter interactions in MATBG and enable resonant optical spectroscopy of moiré bands down to millikelvin temperatures.
summary: This work reports the first FIR spectroscopy of interacting moiré bands in MATBG using a novel millikelvin platform. By combining experiment with the Topological Heavy-Fermion model, the authors revealed characteristic resonances arising from strong light-matter coupling between itinerant and localized electrons. This provides fundamental insight into correlated electronic states in twisted 2D materials.
main_problem: Optical spectroscopy of interacting moiré bands in the far-infrared (FIR) regime has been largely unexplored due to extreme experimental challenges.
main_result: The study observed characteristic FIR resonances in MATBG, showing that light-matter interaction is governed by itinerant topological electrons acting as an 'antenna' coupled to localized heavy fermions.
method: The research combines new millikelvin FIR spectroscopy measurements with theoretical modeling using the Topological Heavy-Fermion (THF) model.
model_or_system: The system is Magic Angle Twisted Bilayer Graphene (MATBG), whose physics is modeled by the THF framework, which incorporates Hubbard interactions for localized heavy fermions and topological character from itinerant light fermions.
key_observables: FIR resonances, photovoltage ($	ext{V}_{	ext{ph}}$) spectra, transport characteristics ($	ext{R}_{	ext{xx}}$), and spectral weight development at low energies.
important_parameters: Filling factor ($v$), magnetic field ($B$), temperature ($T$), on-site Coulomb energy, and various coupling constants within the THF model (e.g., $W_1, W_3, U_1$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that itinerant topological electrons couple strongly to the optical field, and the THF model provides a practical route to compute the optical response.
figures_summary: Figures show FIR spectra mapping photovoltage vs. filling factor/bias current; theoretical calculations illustrate resonance dependence on magnetic field and strain ($\sigma(\omega)$).
paper_structure: The paper establishes the experimental gap, presents measurements using a new millikelvin platform to observe resonances in MATBG, develops the THF model to explain these findings, and analyzes parameter sensitivity across different doping regimes.
why_interesting: The strong coupling between optical fields and emergent many-body modes in flat bands provides a clean platform for studying light-matter interaction in strongly correlated electronic systems, relevant to quantum optics and open quantum systems dynamics.
